# `tpm attest`

@include 'alerts/enterprise-only.mdx'

Attest the local TPM to Vault and save a TPM-bound client certificate.

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```shell-session
$ vault tpm attest [flags]

$ vault tpm attest [-help | -h]
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

## Description

`vault tpm attest` runs a hardware-attested, two-phase enrollment protocol
(`gentpmcert`) with Vault using the local TPM, and gets a client TLS certificate
from the TPM auth method. The TPM must already be enrolled in the namespace of
the auth method mount. The private key stays in the TPM. The command writes only
key references and the certificate to the state directory. It creates the
directory, and any missing parent directories, if it does not exist. The files are:

- `ak.blob`
- `app.blob`
- `client.crt`
- `ca_chain.pem`
- `client-key.json`

Refer to
[Attestation state directory](/vault/docs/auth/tpm#attestation-state-directory)
for the contents of each file. To authenticate with the certificate, run
[`vault login -method=tpm`](/vault/docs/commands/login) with the same
`-tpm-state-dir` and the `role_name` of the role you attested against.

<Tip title="Related API endpoints">

  BeginTPMCertificateIssuance - [`POST:/auth/tpm/role/{role_name}/gentpmcert/begin`](/vault/api-docs/auth/tpm#begin-tpm-certificate-issuance)

  FinishTPMCertificateIssuance - [`POST:/auth/tpm/role/{role_name}/gentpmcert/finish`](/vault/api-docs/auth/tpm#finish-tpm-certificate-issuance)

</Tip>

## Examples

Attest the local TPM against the `my-role` role and save the files to `/private`:

```shell-session
$ vault tpm attest -role-name=my-role -tpm-state-dir=/private
Attestation successful. Certificate valid until: Sat, 16 Jan 2027 17:00:00 UTC
```

Attest the local TPM with a custom certificate subject:

```shell-session
$ vault tpm attest -role-name=my-role -tpm-state-dir=/private \
    -cert-subject-CN=server-01.example.com \
    -cert-subject-O="Example Corp"
```

Authenticate with the issued certificate:

```shell-session
$ vault login -method=tpm -tpm-state-dir=/private role_name=my-role
```
